primer.title: A value that is one of several shapes
body: An `enum` value is exactly one of its variants, and a variant may carry data. `match` must cover every variant; patterns can take the data apart as they match.
`Option<T>` is an ordinary enum: `Some(T)` or `None`. There is no null, and an `Option<u16>` is **not** a `u16` — you must say what happens for `None` (`match`, `if let`, `unwrap_or`, `?`).
Matching **by value** moves data out of the matched value. `Some(p) => …` moves the inner value into `p`; match on a reference (`match &opt`) to only look.
Patterns nest: `while let Some(Some(n)) = stack.pop()` keeps looping only while `pop` returns an item *and* that item is itself `Some`.

code: let (mut w, mut h, mut x, mut quit) = (0, 0, 0, false);

options.rationale: The second `Resize` overwrites the first. `Quit` sets the flag, so the loop breaks before the last `Move` is handled.
`quit` is checked at the top of every iteration. After `Quit`, the loop breaks before `Move(99, 99)` is matched.
Both `Resize` messages arrive before `Quit`, and the later one wins.
`Move(new_x, _)` binds the *first* field. `_` ignores the second.
Hour 9 gives `Some(5)`, 22 gives `Some(0)`, and 25 gives `None`, which `unwrap_or(1)` turns into 1: 5 + 0 + 1.
`Some(0)` is not `None`. An `Option` holding zero is still `Some`.
`unwrap_or` never panics — the argument is the fallback for `None`.

exercises.prompt: This does not compile. What does the compiler object to?

options.text: E0369: `+` cannot be applied to `Option<u16>` on line 7
options.rationale: An `Option<u16>` is not a number. The value has to be taken out first, deciding what `None` means.
Rust does not unwrap an `Option` implicitly, even when it is obviously `Some` at runtime.

options.text: It compiles, and would panic only if the result were `None`
options.rationale: There is no implicit unwrap to panic. The mismatch is caught at compile time.

options.text: E0308: the `if` and `else` branches on line 2 have different types
options.rationale: `Some(5)` and `None` are both `Option<u16>`; the return type settles `None`'s type.

exercises.prompt: Tap the line the compiler rejects.
exercises.rationale: Line 15 uses `optional_point` after the pattern `Some(p)` on line 11 moved the `Point` out of it (E0382, "partially moved").

lineRationales.11: Binding `p` by value moves the `Point` out of the `Option` — which is legal. The error is reported at the later use. Matching on `&optional_point` would only borrow.
lineRationales.10: `match` by itself does not move anything; the patterns inside it decide that.
lineRationales.1: `derive(Debug)` is what makes `{:?}` possible at all. `Point` is not `Copy`, which is why the move matters.

exercises.fallbackRationale: That line compiles. Look for where the `Point` is moved out, then for a later use of its owner.

options.rationale: The fourth `pop` returns `Some(None)`. It does not match `Some(Some(n))`, so the loop ends — but the `None` element has already been popped.
The pattern is tested on the *result* of `pop()`. By the time it fails to match, the element is gone from the vector.
`pop` removes from the end, so the last pushed item comes out first.
A pattern that fails to match ends a `while let`.
